original_question: What is a complete characterization of K4-free bricks, meaning bricks for which the complete graph K4 is not a conformal minor? Equivalently, which bricks fail to be K4-based under the paper's definition that a matching covered graph is J-based exactly when J is a conformal minor of it, and J-free otherwise?
target_in_paper: Section 1.7.3, Unsolved Problem 1.30: Characterize K4-free bricks.
correct_elements: Your draft identifies the exact paper-level target: the class of bricks for which K4 is not a conformal minor. It also correctly uses the paper's J-based/J-free language and correctly treats 'K4-free' and 'not K4-based' as equivalent notions under the paper's definition.
missing_details: The paper's official formulation is an open problem, not a proved theorem: it is stated exactly as 'Characterize K4-free bricks.'
To be fully stand-alone, the question should define a brick as a nonbipartite matching covered graph with no nontrivial tight cuts.
It should define a matching covered graph as a connected loopless graph of order at least two in which every edge is admissible.
It should unpack 'K4 is a conformal minor of G' by saying that some bi-subdivision H of K4 is a subgraph of G and G - V(H) has a perfect matching.
It should define a bi-subdivision as replacing each edge by a path of odd length, equivalently subdividing an edge by an even number of vertices.

For paper-faithful scope, it helps to note why the problem is posed at the brick level: by Theorem 1.29, for any cubic brick J, a matching covered graph is J-free if and only if each of its bricks is J-free; this applies to J = K4.
The nearby partial result recorded in the paper is only the simple planar case: Theorem 1.32 characterizes simple planar K4-free bricks.
refined_question: Among loopless graphs, characterize all bricks G, where a brick is a nonbipartite matching covered graph with no nontrivial tight cuts, such that K4 is not a conformal minor of G; equivalently, determine exactly which bricks are K4-free, meaning that there is no bi-subdivision H of K4 with H a subgraph of G and G - V(H) admitting a perfect matching.
equivalent_formulation: Characterize all bricks G that are not K4-based under the paper's terminology; equivalently, characterize all bricks G for which no bi-subdivision of K4 occurs as a conformal subgraph of G.
justification: This is the exact target because Section 1.7.3 first defines conformal minors and the J-based/J-free terminology, then proves the brick-reduction statement for cubic J in Theorem 1.29, and immediately afterward states Unsolved Problem 1.30 as 'Characterize K4-free bricks.' Your draft matches that official formulation closely. The paper's later main equivalence is about solid bricks and C6-bar-free bricks, not about replacing Problem 1.30 with a different K4-question, and the only explicit K4 characterization supplied in the paper is the simple planar special case in Theorem 1.32.
